tips.comment: In a nineteen-runner field over this demanding 1m4f course, the start can be key. Ryan Moore was able to overcome a bad draw in stall 1 when winning aboard City Of Troy last year. He will likely adopt more aggressive tactics aboard DELACROIX this year, who will come out of stall 14. All four of his career wins to date have come from prominent early positions, albeit in much smaller fields. This Dubawi colt comes here having won on both of his starts this season, seeing out the 1m2f at Leopardstown strongly on both occasions. Those two races were both won by Aiden O’Brien-trained Galileo and High Chaparral en route to their Derby victories. He’s versatile on the ground, having raced on a range of surfaces from Soft to Good to Firm. He steps up to 1m4f for the first time today, but the manner of his two most recent wins, along with the positive words of the trainer, would suggest that there is little to worry about in that respect.

Unbeaten Pride Of Arras is one of the least exposed colts in the field having run once as a two year old and then winning the Dante at York a month ago where he led in the last two furlongs and stayed on strongly. Drawn high close to Delacroix he will have to find cover to avoid being trapped wide throughout if he is being held up until the straight.
Stamoina to prove, but did win well going away last time out at Newmarket. There could be more to come now stepping up in trip. Won't want rain.

Sparkling form as a 2-year-old and won the Acomb Stakes Group 3 at York in eye-catching style and kept finding more. Disappointed in the Dante when never settling and a bit buzzy throughout the race, eventually finishing 6th, but will surely come on for that race. Discarded by Ryan Moore but has said nothing between the O'Brien horses and a difficult choice, and Colin Keane takes the ride.

O'Brien has a remarkable record in this race and fields three. All have good chances, but Lambourn has as much as the others at a larger price. Winner of the Chester Vase last time out, he has proven stamina and will enjoy a well-paced race. Well drawn and ticks many trend boxes of previous winners.

On form has no chance but being parachuted last minute into the Derby after an unbeaten in three start to career in a race named in honour of the late great Aga Khan would make even an uneducated form student like me sit up and take notice. Surely from the embarrassment of riches connections own we all have to take note. Looks a well balanced sort who won last time at the left handed Saint-Cloud in good style on good to soft ground and looks likely to stay this far stepping up in trip. Improving sort and ground should be fine so in a very open race could be the one to keep late rapid improvement going and go well. Took 16's earlier in the week and note is being nibbled at and given that I don't fancy loads in here looks a cracking each way bet at the very least. Wouldn't be surprised if he goes off at single figures and if handling the razzmatazz on just fourth start looks a cracking EW punt at the very least.
This should be a wide-open race with decent odds for an each-way bet. I would go for the John Gosden-trained Damysus, who was runner-up in the Dante Stakes last time out.

Stanhope Gardens looks a big price on last season's neck defeat by Delacroix at Newmarket last October. He had a delayed start to this season and won as a 2/11 shot should at Salisbury two weeks ago in his only start. He was strong at the finish there and should stay 12 furlongs. At this price, he is a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.

A J P O'Brien trained 3 year old who has finished in the first three 5 times from 5 starts on turf, including winning a French Group 1 race in October when finishing 1st of 3 over 10 furlongs at Saint-Cloud on heavy ground. Regular jockey Dylan McMonagle rides today with a good chance over 12 furlongs on good to soft going.

New Ground was closing hard when last seen. The two horses ahead have hardly franked the form in the French Derby, but the horse in behind was a solid 5th there, and this horse had also chased home the French Derby 2nd as well so there is some sort of substance to the form. I felt it interesting enough that this horse has been supplemented even though Juddmonte already had a runner in here (who has already been beaten by Delacroix). Stall 17 is the major negative, although the last two runnings of this with 18-19 runners have seen horses win from stall 14. I’m willing to ignore it, and all of his negatives are baked into his price.

Hasn't hit top form yet as a three year old but ran respectably when 5th in the Dante at York last time behind the likely favourite for this race. Was keeping on without getting a vigorous ride and the extra distance could see a much stronger performance. One to consider.

Lazy Griff could be worth an Each Way 4 Places as he won a G3 in France in September and was a decent second on the return from a break last month in a G3 at Chester. He should improve now second up, plus I like having Christophe Soumillon in the saddle for this.

A very easy winner of both starts last season over 7f and 1 mile. Good effort on seasonal return when only beaten 4 lengths in the Group 2 Dante over 1m2f at York last month on first start for 7 months. Should come on for that run and will be suited if the forecast rain arrives and the connections have had 2 big priced frame finishers in this race since 2021.

This one could well be the little diamond in the rough this year at a huge 150-1. The owner also has Green Storm (also backed each way), and this owner/trainer combo had one run well at a price last year. Others have run in much higher grade races than this, but this is proven over this distance, unlike most of these. Although there are quite a few runners this year, it means more likely an upset. Realistically looking for a place, but if running like Chester, it will get out from a poor draw to lead and could hold on with stamina assured.

Plenty of outsiders get placed in this great race, and a few have even won, including in recent years Wings of Eagles in 2017, who won at 40/1. This horse fits the Dosage profiles of previous winners and has talented Billy Loughnane riding in his first Derby. His OR of 107 is 10th best but would only need to improve 5lb to be joint 5th best. Charlie Johnston has commented that the horse has been targeted here for a long time.

With an official rating of 114, DOCKLANDS is top-rated in this field. He comes here on the back of a second in a Queen Anne Trial at Ascot (8f, Good to Firm). He finished ½l behind the winner (Sardinian Warrior) that day, clocking the fastest final furlong in the field. The winner that day has since finished a length behind Sosie in the Group 1 Prix d’Ispahan, and so that form looks particularly strong. His best form has come over the straight mile at Ascot, but he has had experience around left-handed tracks, and the Epsom straight gives him enough time to find his stride to come from his preferred held-up position. With the 3lbs age allowance, this five-year-old has a bit in hand on official ratings and therefore looks like the one to side with.

They're forecast rain tonight (Friday) and Richard Hannon's 4yo can't have enough. He was out of his league in the Lockinge on fast ground and is better judged on his Earl Of Sefton (Gp3) win at the Guineas meeting on more suitable going.

Royal Playwright appears to be the unexposed angle in this race, and he becomes particularly interesting as the only three-year-old in the field, receiving a significant age allowance. A winner on debut at Salisbury, he continued to progress with placed efforts in both the Royal Lodge and the Solario Stakes, before finding Group 1 company a bit too demanding. He was being prepared for a run in the Dante, but a wide draw compromised his chances, and he was not given a hard race. The drop back to a mile and a more favourable starting position should help. He is out of Arabian Queen, who won at this meeting, and he is likely to enjoy some cut in the ground. He looks a solid each-way contender at around 6/1.

ICE MAX has to be a player for the powerful Kark Burke yard with rain set to fall overnight. That would strengthen this four year old's chance whilst counting against others and with a reappearance sighter behind him when the yard were not in such good form he appeals.

I've picked holes in all of these but something has to win and fill the frame and though Persica looks the obvious one looks too short a price for me given last run in the Lockinge when last of the field. The German raider catches my eye as a three time Group 3 winner on good to soft ground each time in native land and could go well here. Christophe Soumillion booked and is the fly in the ointment in a very tricky puzzle of a race. Showed a good attitude to battle back to win narrowly last time at Dusdledorf and can go well here if handling the track. EW chance and price to my eye as trio and ground look spot on and thus doesn't look the deepest race.

Runner-up in this race last year on seasonal debut on good to soft ground. Has the benefit of a prep race this year, having run over a mile at Ascot at the end of April, and likely targeted for this race.

Royal Playwright winning this would pain me, but he could get stuck in behind and have to do this the hard way. And whilst getting weight all round, I just can’t back him again. The one that made minor appeal was Cairo, who went well at a big price last time. He possibly just got going a bit too soon, but back almost a furlong in trip can bode well given how well he was placed at the furlong point. Prior to that, the horse that beat him had chased home the classy Rebel’s Romance, so there is substance enough to that form. Liberty Lane in behind has also won since, so there is substance to the form. He’s unexposed on ground worse than good, being 2/3 a place on it. 6/6 a place going left-handed, he’s a capable ex-O’Brien horse that is yet to make a mark for this trainer. But with a lack of a real standout in here, I think his chance of being involved is way overstated, especially given he meets Persica on 10lbs better terms here, who is 5/2 and beat him 2-3L at Windsor last August.

One of the two favourites will likely win this contest, but I find it too difficult to choose one of them. So I'll be having an each-way go at a big prize. Tyrrhenian Sea ran much better than the result at Ascot, as his jockey put him in no man's land between the clear leader and the rest of the pack. They went too fast, and the ground wasn't to his liking either. This horse has his best form on the all-weather, but he hasn't gotten a fair chance on turf in quite some time, which he should be getting here.
Ruby's Profit is in great form this season thus far. She won with more in hand than the official margin at Goodwood and holds several of these on that run. Could once again lead from the start.

The two at the top of the weights arrive in their best form yet and can fight this out. I think Against The Wind can win. Kevin Ryan is a master of training top sprinters and may well have doubled up last time had the jockey been able to keep him straight at the end. The hanging cost him, but a 3rd in a big field and big race is good form. Likes to blast out and make it. Couldn't be at a better 5 furlongs than this to try that.

The 3yo filly took a nice step forward on her return two weeks ago from a 9 month break. She was a close 2nd of 10 over this 5f trip, staying on strong from off the pace, earning a huge RPR rating. Every chance she can improve for the run. Good jockey booking and can be a big player if racing closer to the pace.

Blinky negated his rail draw at Chester by getting a poor start but still chased down Ruby's Profit, finishing in 3rd, whilst Ruby's Profit could only finish 2nd in the end but went on to win at Goodwood. They met at level weights at Chester, and Blinky now gets nine pounds. Drawn in 18 and 17, they should be close at the finish.

Taking a chance on Richard Fahey to do it again with Stormy Impact chanced in this 3yo dash. I think she’s a big price given her sole run on ground with soft in the going was behind a now 100 rated horse. She’ll need a career best, but that run on GS deserves a watch back as she absolutely breezed into the race in the final furlong there. It seems highly likely plenty of rain will arrive, which I think is a big plus to her chances. If she can break well, I’d hope Fentiman just lets her roll towards the pace on the far rail.
Naanas Sparkle has been in the first four home on the last six occasions and should give another good attempt here with a bonus five places on offer for each-way backers.

Inexperienced filly but could well be a bit better than a handicapper in time given form shown so far. Made a pleasing debut staying on well to be fourth at York to Betty Clover and that one was a good fourth in the Duty Free last season and has now placed at Group 2,3 and Listed level. Cut no ice on second start but caught the eye on seasonal debut at Wolverhampton when third in a novice fillies stakes. The second and fifth from that race have both won since and the actual winner and fourth have both been narrowly beaten at Windsor since too. Form stacking up and can go well on handicap debut and what catches my eye is that has an entry for Catterick on Tuesday but comes here instead despite owner having two other runners too. Could have a squeak at a decent price.
Acrisius is trained by northern trainer M D Easterby, who has two in the race. He has a nice low weight, and the jockey takes off another 5 lb.

GOLD STAR HERO may have a decent draw high in this five furlong sprint. He comes from a shrewd yard and assuming hev is effective on the forecast soft ground he was aimed high last year and could prove well treated in this handicap division.

CONVO reunites with Tom Marquand who rode this filly for her former trainer. She was pitched into Group 3 company in the Albany at Royal Ascot for Amy Murphy last year and she may have needed more time potentially peaking as a sprinter now.

This horse looks exactly the type that has been laid out for this. There's plenty of rain in the forecast and on breeding, you'd have to say that the horse could well improve for a first-ever run on softish ground. The trainer has only had the horse for one race when he wasn't knocked about and gets to race off the same mark here. I've been hugely impressed by the jockey booked recently, and his first-time booking also catches the eye. The horse's 2nd in a decent novice race at Sandown is the piece of form which gives him a major chance here, and when the rain gets into the ground, the high numbers should be favored, so 16 of 18 is ideal.

Tees Aggregates ran pretty tamely at Leicester on Tuesday. Was fairly weak in the market there and not asked too many questions. That makes sense as a prep run for this race. Previously, kept on well to win at Catterick in early May from OR66 and runs from very low in the handicap here, carrying just 8 stone 2 pounds. In receipt of lumps of weight from some of these. Drawn 15 which is pretty good. Trainer Adrian Nicholls (SR 25%) in good form. Sean D Bowen rides.

I'm not a huge fan of Epsom with its quirky up, down turning into a camber at the finish, but it does mean that course form is a big plus. ELOUISES PRINCE doesn't have that course form but has shown great speed and balance in winning twice last season. A huge price for one that looks very capable of running a big race. Did run a bit of a stinker on seasonal debut at York, but that's easily forgiven as it blew very hard and likely that will have blown cobwebs away.

Royal Dress was extremely unlucky in this race last year when finishing a close 3rd as she was continually denied a clear run to challenge for over a furlong from over 2f out and would probably have won otherwise. She ran respectably in a Group 2 first time out and should go close again.

Has 1 win and 2 second place finishes from 4 career starts and, being the only 3-year-old in the field, gets a 12 lb allowance from the whole of the field. Has run well in both starts this year and a big chance with the in-form Oisin Murphy riding.

In a field not exempt from threats, Skellet emerges as the best candidate with great chances. The selection raced during last season at the highest level, finishing with a remarkable sequence of place and win results. Rossa Ryan on the saddle will help its cause.

A tricky opener, and a small chance on Sirona who was a bit too free off the front end on seasonal reappearance. She eventually got run down by 3 race fit rivals, but it was to her credit that she only really faded in the last 50 yards. With that run under her belt, a few lbs better with Bright Thunder, and Ryan Moore in the saddle, she can hopefully latch onto pace on her outside to get a decent position here. Any rain will do her chances no harm, though my main concern is her getting home if they go too hard here with a possible contested pace.

The Group 3 Princess Elizabeth Stakes looks wide open, and Bright Thunder represents a bit of value at around 9/1. She has been campaigned consistently at Group 3 and Listed level, including several trips to France last season, probably in search of ground with some cut, winning a Listed race at Chantilly around this time last year. She will encounter similar conditions today, she is well drawn in stall four, and tends to race prominently, which was the winning tactic for every runner at this venue yesterday. At the current prices, she looks worth an each way bet with bookies paying four places.
With conditions likely to change tomorrow to no good ground, now turning soft. With regular winning jockey in the saddle, win bet.

SPIRITUAL represents a leading yard who show stats of 8/28 { 29% } with runners sents to this venue always respected and a high drw over this trip on the predicted soft ground could be the best place to start from. Value player.

Very tricky opener but this one on stable debut shouldn't be totally ruled out. Won 4 from 8 last season including on seasonal debut and ended up a Listed winner at Ascot on final start. Yard had a winner and a couple of places here yesterday and a winner up at Doncaster too, so are in decent form. This likeable sort has won on the all weather, fast, good and soft ground so is very adaptable. Has a squeak as goes well fresh and though has to improve has a good attitude and could surprise a few here. What I like about her is the fact she won the Listed October Stakes at Ascot on final start last season and last year's winner of this Breege was beaten a head in the 2023 renewal of that race herself. Must of been aimed at this and is a big price.

Talented individual who picked up a nice race at Haydock last summer, beating the very progressive American Affair in the process. Solid effort behind the same rival on reappearance before below par at Chester last time, but that is readily excused. So, should go very well this afternoon.

A competitive race, but Jm Jungle looks to have a great chance. He has run really well in good races all three starts this season. He ran okay on his only start at the track and won't mind the softening ground. With the extra place, he looks worth a bet.

Two races ago, Spartan Arrow won over course and distance by just over two lengths. Next time out, he ran disappointingly at York. Carries an extra seven pounds since his last win. Holly Doyle is again doing the steering. Hopefully, he will bounce back and run a good race.

A wide-open looking race. Distance winner off only a 1 lb higher mark on soft ground. Ran well in his last two starts and is dropping down to a good mark again. Richard Fahey brings only a select number of horses down from his Yorkshire stable.

Democracy Dilemma nearly won this race last year but he was headed late on by Dream Composer and he faces that rival again today. He has winning form on good to soft ground and if the expected rain showers appear he also has won on soft and heavy.

Existent has only won once on turf, and that was as a two-year-old in 2020. His only other wins on the all-weather were two in January and February 2022. However, he continues to run competitively, finishing 2nd in his last four races, which includes here behind Spartan Arrow in April. Rose Dawes takes his weight below eight stone.

I usually don't take multiple runners in the same race, but I can't see anything else winning other than these two. Fair Wind had a nice campaign last season until he refused to race all of a sudden. He has since finished last on his reappearance, but there were excuses for that. He still looks well handicapped to me, but he'll need to prove he's still capable of performing at this level.

The shrewd trainer puts his 7lb claiming apprentice up here, and they've been landing some decent prizes between them this season. The jockey was placed on his only other ride here, and the horse has won on his only other race over C&D (as a 4yo). The horse has slipped to his lowest handicap run in 5 races now, and it's now or never. We get to find out if the horse is in the handicapper's grip still, or, as I suspect, the trainer has been targeting this for a while and gets the horse racing off a competitive mark now with the bonus of a further 7lb taken off his back.

A very tentative vote on Desert Cop in the dash, who may not appreciate this if too much rain arrives. Cosgrave has won with 2 of his last 3 runs over 5f here, whilst also being 3/4 a place with 2 winners at 6f. Get It has put a fair gloss on his latest win in Bahrain, and Kodi Lion has franked that form since too. A classy 3yo, he’s been hard to win with since, and a mark of 100 doesn’t look overly kind. He’s drawn bang on the rail though, and Cosgrave can be lethal from the front if he can get this horse out of the stalls smartly. He’s only had four runs over the minimum distance now, including a Group 1 sixth, and with that recent franked form, I’m chancing him as a bit of a wildcard in here outside of the intertwined form of the others.

The Bell Conductor looks a fair play in the Epsom Dash. Well drawn in stall 17 just off the inside rail. Second start for Ivan Furtado having left Craig Lidster pre-season. Coming in for market support. Three wins from 18 races on turf. Ran fifth in this race last year from a rating of 97 and runs off 94 today. Tom Eaves rides. Preference for soft but did win last year on good ground.

RHYTHM N HOOVES is running very consistently at the moment so is considered with the extra places here. Stepped up to this grade the last twice on turf, at Goodwood and Windsor. Fourth or better in last ten races and if anything is getting better. Can make a stronger case for this than some others at shorter prices.

Nogo's Dream is five pounds out of the handicap, but there have been a few big-priced winners of this race recently. Arriving on the back of some solid form, it should be a lively pick for each-way backers here.

One of five in the race for the Cowell yard. Made stable debut in August and improved for WS, winning twice over the winter. Last two runs on turf: 4/11 at Epsom, 3/8 at Goodwood. Has a handy draw in 1.

The trainer has had three placed in this race in recent years, including this horse. Arrives in good form and has won off higher marks on the all-weather before. Also interesting, cheekpieces are applied for only the second time, and has a jockey he gets on well with. Can win this race with such a low weight.

A 4-time winner who has only finished out of the frame once in the last 9 starts. Won over this course and distance last September on soft ground and won well over this trip last time out at Chester last month, so looks a leading contender.

Valvano is a progressive 4-year-old with form reading well in context. Trained by Beckett and ridden by Hector Crouch, he’s a grinder who keeps finding more. Has placed consistently and now meets ideal conditions. Looks very solid and has less question marks than others near the top of the market.

I'm a big fan of trainer Dylan Cunha, and his 5yo looks progressive at this trip, despite the 7lb rise for his win over CD in the Great Metropolitan here in April. He was third in this last year when ridden to get the trip, and with Oisin Murphy in the plate, there'll be much more confidence this year.

Candyman Stan has shown a lot of promise for trainer Andrew Balding (SR 18%). Has won three of just six starts with all three wins coming at (very close to) the 1m4f trip. Has gone clear of his field on a couple of occasions. His last win was at Class 2 level and must continue to progress with a 5lbs rise but has looked pretty decent so far. Jason Watson, having ridden him to success the last twice, retains the ride.

There could be enough rain to make the going soft enough for Miller Spirit, who won five times last flat season and also over hurdles. His last two wins on the flat were both on heavy to complete a three-timer, the first two over course and distance. Gary and Josh Moore run three horses, but if back to last season's form after two lesser runs on good, which has dropped his mark back to 94 from 97, he should at least be placed.

This horse should be well handicapped if finding the right scenario and right conditions. This could be it, and down 2 lbs with an added 5 taken off, he makes even more appeal. He split a pair of 94-98 rated horses for O’Brien in the only race that he’s seen conditions. Owes Ethan good, so the rain that’s got into the ground can be a major plus. The fact he’s a full brother to Library also makes that case. Off a feather 8 st 2 lbs, I think there’s a high chance he stays here. A watch back of his last race showed a horse not ridden to his true potential. He’s 1 lb better off with Candyman Stan here, who is half the price.

Dream Harder had not won in a long time until winning at Chester last week in a C4. But earlier this year, he was twice running to third off an 87 in C2. With today's 85, he could be worth an EW 5P chance.

A mark of 100 looks high enough in a handicap as competitive as this, but Maxi King spent most of 2024 running in pattern races, and the handicaps he did contest wouldn't have given him the best chance of winning due to race conditions. Soft ground is a huge plus for him, and he goes really well fresh, having won off breaks of 136 and 386 days on his last two reappearances. He's 2 lbs lower than when 8th at Doncaster in November, but crucially, I think this could be the time to catch him. With plenty of pace on offer, the setup of the race looks ideal too.

There are 8 horses in this field that won LTO, so I'm expecting a competitive race tomorrow. Thankfully, my selection is among the LTO winners. This horse has serious ability, and if he can overcome the steep raised mark (+7lbs) and going up in class, then he has a chance.

Jedd O'Keefe trains at Middleham in North Yorkshire and sends Something on the 526 miles round trip to race at Epsom in The Northern Dancer Handicap. Something, I am told by a yard contact, has been working well and won last time out at Ripon. My contact says Jedd is 'bullish' about the horse who steps up in grade here. He has a task bigger than he has met before. Jedd sending him this distance makes an each-way appeal with Hollie Doyle onboard.

I’m going to take a wild swing on the old boy here in TORCELLO at 40/1 with 5 places on offer. The veteran by Born To Sea is a course winner, coming on his only start here back in 2019 on heavy ground and it looks as though he’ll get soft ground today. He absolutely thrives under these conditions (33% SR, A/E 2.55 on good to soft or worse) and the trip is of no concern (28% SR, A/E 2.5 in the UK) plus he won on reappearance last season, albeit in a lower grade. The gelding isn’t the most consistent but is running off his lowest mark for a few years to make life easier and a number of positive stats boost claims; most notable being S Lycett’s 24% SR (A/E 1.78) with runners keeping to the same trip and D Gilbert’s 21% SR (A/E 1.84) with Irish-born runners.

Chartwell Jock represents value with Oisin Murphy booked. From the Balding yard, he’s a sprinter with improving form and solid figures. The market has respected him, and he looks likely to get a nice trip. With a strong pace expected, his turn-of-foot will be a serious asset in the finish.

Four career runs for the 3yo colt, form 11-23. Very possible that the trip and fast ground was against him when 3rd three weeks ago. Better judged on his handicap debut during April on his return from a 5-month break, 2nd of 5 that day over this 10f trip on slower ground. Beaten a length and clear of the rest - the winner was a smart unbeaten Charlie Appleby runner, now rated 98. The selection is on a handy-looking mark, room for improvement, and is facing rivals rated 79-89.

Won nicely on debut as a 2-year-old at Ayr and equaled that form on the next start there too on softish ground, so should handle conditions today. Hasn't set the world alight since, but the yard is in much better form now and they have gelded this son of New Bay. It's that pedigree that catches my eye, as the sire was responsible for last year's winner of this race, Persica, and the dam won over 1m2f and 1m3.5f, so the step up in trip looks sure to suit. Looks the one to beat for me.

Meblesh looks the one to be on here. After a promising debut over an inadequate 7f at Doncaster, he was too keen 12 days later at Newbury after being stuck wide with no cover. He looked a progressive colt back there 22 days ago & I know he's well thoughtof by connections.

War Hawk won last week at Chester and should cope with a five pound rise in his mark and get at least a place here with a decent draw near the rail to tuck in behind Cayman Dancer if he leads from the inside stall.
Won really well at Goodwood last time out, and this track should suit in the follow-up attempt. Also, the six-pound penalty for that win might not stop this one from running well.

Love Talk looks interesting at a big price. He has top weight but that is not a disadvantage at Epsom and he seems to show his best form in soft conditions and with the weather forecast for heavy rain in the south it could be very soft by tomorrow.

Eye Of Dubai still looks well handicapped on a mark of 90 (carries 8 stone 13 pounds). Twice won 6f handicaps on soft ground at Class 2 level last year off OR84 and OR87. Only four years old so further improvement pretty possible. Makes first start this season here and has arguably been waiting for soft ground. Smart grey, bred for sprinting by Havana Grey out of a mare by Orpen. Solid form record with three wins and seven places in 13 starts. Early market support. Jason Hart rides for John & Sean Quinn. Looks a fair play at 11-2.
Richard Fahey's 7yo has become a regular in this race, and much will depend on how much rain they get on Friday evening and throughout the day on Saturday. The more, the better.

Bounced back from a mediocre Bahrain campaign with an impressive victory at Ascot last time out. Up 7 lbs in deeper waters but has form off similar marks and should appreciate conditions here more than most.

SOLAR ACCLAIM is better off at the weights with some he has faced previously and he has an Irish 7lb claiming apprentice aboard. This could be interesting and there could be something to read into that , so the value play with a spin behind him could be this runner.

Good ew chance with 4 places on offer. The stable has done well in this race and this one looks to have another good chance. Won LTO and up 5lb but may still have another win in him if he's in the same mood.

INTERVENTION is a bit risky for win purposes, but has shown some ability in recent outings. He doesn't look out of place in this grade or from this weight and we've potentially got the elements here for a big run from a big price. Distance shouldn't be an issue and even though he didn't fare too well in this last year, I'll give him another chance.

Purest Time was a decent performer when trained previously in France.
Had no chance last time out from a poor draw at Chester and much more is expected here with the return to 6 furlongs a plus.

Totally exposed sort but has back class and was a Group 3 winner in Ireland and must be noted it was only last May when touched off in a Listed event at Naas trying to given an Aidan O'Brien horse rated 111 at the time 3lb. Ran behind a couple who go in the 2.45 when last of 8 on stable debut so it'll be interesting to see how they go but could improve on second start for yard. Adaptable regards ground and it catches my eye has a Wokingham entry at Royal Ascot so connections must think is a decent sort. Looks on a fair mark on best form and might surprise a few here. Young jockey did ride a winner on this Derby day card last season and this one has a squeak.

Three runs this year for the 4yo filly. Decent run in a US Grade 1 during April. Beaten just a nk in a good looking Group 3 four weeks ago. Her fitness should be spot on now. She was a runner-up in a Group 1 last summer. She looks a standout at this Listed level.

Stop The Cavalry is a lightly raced filly who has won first time out in both of the seasons she has raced. Her form looks pretty strong, and she will likely be still improving. Her very close third in a Longchamp Listed race at the end of last season looks a good line of form, potentially strong enough to win this.

It's interesting Fiery Lucy travels from Ireland for this listed contest. She was runner up in a group race at Leopardstown last time. Her trainer often gets his runners well prepared when travelling. A win is no given but she's too interesting to ignore.

Hasn’t won for a while but ran a cracker last time at York under a 7lb claimer on board. Finished the race off strongly having been short of room two out from a mark of 94. Is back in listed company now under a top jockey and is well worth a second look.

The yard is in excellent form, and the horse is in good form also. Only beaten by a neck at Longchamp in a listed race over in France on reappearance and should be in the mix to win this one. Each-way bet advised.
The selection is bidding for a hat trick with a very good chance to complete it in this company. King's Crown looks the best of the rest.
Competitive type with mid-field finishes. May sneak into the places if the leaders fade. Represents good each-way value in a weak field.

Veteran, who picked up a 7th career victory when striking over course and distance in October, mostly struggled since and was well beaten last time. But has slipped back down to that last winning mark (has won the last twice off 48), so is of interest on that basis.

Plenty of miles on the clock for the 7yo but he does have three AW wins this year and is still running to a good level. Back from a 2 month break last month with a good turf run, only beaten 2L - didn't have a lot of room in the later stages of that race. Facing much lower rated rivals now, a 2lb lower mark, capable apprentice booked for the ride who can claim a useful 5lb. He ran a couple of respectable turf races this time last year while rated a huge 16lb higher than his current mark. He looks overpriced.
Showed promise when finishing 2nd at Ripon last month but struggled next time in listed company at York. Should find this easier, and with improvement likely, should be there or thereabouts.

Filly Foden ??' Improving 2-year-old filly with consistent form, placing in all three starts. Shows good speed and determination, and now gets the benefit of top jockey Silvestre de Sousa. Handles fast ground well. Faces stronger opposition but has solid claims and could challenge for the win if progressing again.
Was Superb winning LTO in what was only his 2nd outing at Beverley last month. But this will be a much harder test, which is made even harder going up 4 classes tomorrow.

Won on debut over 7f at Newcastle before running 3rd again on the AW, but this time at Southwell, stepping up to a mile. Made his handicap debut on the turf at Newbury last time, kept to that trip, and finished a close-up 3rd. Races off the same mark but in first-time blinkers and looks a major player.

Zarathos ??' Exceptionally consistent 3-year-old who rarely runs a bad race. Always in the mix and handles a range of conditions. Lacks a turn of foot but grinds out strong finishes. Likely to be staying on late and appeals as a reliable each-way contender in a competitive middle-distance handicap.

I’d make CITY OF GOD much shorter than 15/2 for the feature at Musselburgh today and that makes him a decent each way play. Regalian has to overcome his owner’s 10% SR (A/E 0.49) with geldings, meanwhile Zarathos carries a poor FlatStats rating with plenty of negative stats to boot; most damning being D Cunha’s 4% SR (A/E 0.44) with runners coming up in trip. C Johnston’s 6% SR (A/E 0.43) with runners over 9f puts me off Thunder Wonder but a strong case can be made for COG; the colt by Kodiac showed plenty of promise on the AW over the winter, winning on 2nd start and finishing runner-up on his next two. He was then given a few months off before returning in a C2 handicap at Haydock where he ran well enough but looked a touch rusty. The 3yo should come on for the run, the step up in trip should suit here given the sire’s 3/8 record (A/E 2.25) over C&D and S James brings a superb 36% SR (A/E 1.49) at Musselburgh when riding for the K Burke team.

6/8 in a listed Class 1 race in November at Newmarket was a respectable run following on from her first two runs (wins) in Class 4 and 5. She makes her handicap debut today after 7 months off and could surprise a few here and go very close.

Wolverhampton novice winner who is yet to win a handicap but was generally running well until a couple of poor recent efforts. Cheekpieces could be to blame, though, so of interest today with them discarded off this career-low mark.

Last (and only) win came in August 2024 when winning a 7f handicap off a mark of 69 and continued throughout 2024 in good form (running off marks in high 70’s).
Beaten only 1 length (3rd of 12) in his first run of 2025 after a 5 months break, I think we can ignore his latest effort when putting in a run well below capabilities to finish 12½ lengths behind the winner in a Class 4, 6f handicap, so hopefully he can bounce back to form today with an improved performance (running off a mark of 76) in a race that looks a very open handicap

3 times a winner here, twice over course and distance and once over 9 furlongs. Runner-up over a mile here on the 13th of April and should appreciate this return to 7 furlongs. Was declared to run at Ripon on Wednesday but a non-runner and possible that the yard are trying to find the right opportunity for him,and the forecast rain will help.

VINCE LE PRINCE has been good to us in the past and is given a whirl now back to last winning mark. Now 4lbs lighter than when running well on seasonal debut over this trip in April, and there are no concerns over the going. We need to forgive the last couple of runs but maybe the return here is what the doctor ordered.
Chiefman has tumbled down the weights and, having had one prep run this season, just might be ready to strike for astute trainer Mike Smith.

Reservardo ??' Consistent and progressive 3-year-old with strong form, including a win last time out. Regularly hits the frame and seems to be improving with each run. Well-handicapped and suited by the trip and ground. Represents a sharp yard and looks a major threat with winning momentum behind him.
Luna A Inbhir Nis is the in-form sprinter with 3 wins from 4 starts, all over the minimum trip this year. The last win was over this track and trip, and a 6lb rise in ratings looks manageable.

Improvements were not evident for the new yard LTO when only 14th of 22 at York last month. However, that was her first run in about 9 months, to be fair. So, expecting a more competitive effort this time out, which is helped by a drop down in class and a dropped mark.

Top Gun Tina ??' Honest and consistent 5-year-old mare who regularly finishes in the top four. Well-handicapped and running into form, with solid recent efforts suggesting a win could be near. Versatile in running style and suited by trip. Strong each-way contender in a wide-open low-grade handicap.
Could be very interesting. Won this race last year. Should come on for recent return here over mile one. Change of headgear makes things interesting.

The Easterby stable are hitting form currently, two winners at Thirsk on Friday, and My Honey B has had two races to bring her to peak form. She's dropped a fair way down the ratings since she last won, and this looks a good opportunity for her to find a place at least.

Is on a long losing run stretching back to August 2021, when winning a 1m handicap, off a mark of 74.
Consistently finished down the field in 15 runs in 2024 resulting in a 17lbs drop in the handicap, but after returning in May this year after a 5 months break with 2 decent placed efforts over 1m and 1m½f, I don’t think we can ignore this runner as he has been eased another 1lb after his latest effort to a career low mark of 49 and looks worth an EW bet at 15.00 with 4 places on offer
Yet to win on turf but is a 3-time winner on the all-weather. Likely to go well, and if transferring that all-weather form to turf, will have an each-way chance.

SUPERIOR COUNCIL is so well treated on his best form and although he maybe somewhat in decline this is a near-basement level handicap. He has the benefit of a reappearance sighter behind him now taking in his second start for his new scottish yard and he could get involved.

This ex A M Thomson trained 8-year-old gelding has improved since joining his new trainer James Owen. He ran second on his first start over hurdles and followed that up by winning a chase over three miles on good ground at Uttoxeter in his latest start. So, with the five-pound claimer Mr. Alex Chadwick onboard, it looks like another win today.

The model Irun suggests Somespring Special can win this one. This result has been driven by Somespring Special having the highest RPR of this small 4 runner race. It has the second lowest official ranking and goes out carrying slightly less weight than the top 2 in the market. Comes here in good form, with figures of 4012-2 and looks to get over the line first again. Last run 24 days ago and race fitness should not be a concern. The model issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Ile De Jersey doesn't look a natural over fences, and I'm happy to oppose at the price. Mermaids Cave goes over fences for the first time for James Owen, who is in great form. She seems to have improved the last two times since cheekpieces have gone on, and she looks interesting here.

This 5-y-o gelding won over two miles one furlong on good ground in his final race for Irish trainer P M J Doyle at Killarney. So, making his debut for new trainer B I Case with J M Quinlan booked to ride, he looks hard to oppose with conditions in his favour.

Squire Danagher was very disappointing on first run over hurdles for Ben Pauling yard. Did lose a shoe there. Expected to be better than that. Very smart staying pedigree actually, by Derby winner Australia out of a Deep Impact mare. Won four times on the all weather at Dundalk for former yard. Returns to Worcester 2 miles novices hurdle and better is hoped for this time.

Changed tactics successfully when clinching a low-grade handicap chase last month. Not showing the same form a week later, which renders him quite vulnerable returning to hurdles, but with the jockey and trainer performing exceptionally well, an each-way bet at appealing odds of 33/1 looks like a great opportunity.
Has won on all of the last 3 starts, including over this course and distance on the latest outing. Should go well again and holds every chance of keeping that winning run going.

Shantou Express still retains ability at 10 years old as shown in two comeback runs in April and May. Made the frame in 2 out of 3 runs here. Has won at this trip and on various ground. Looks a very solid each-way option in a race where a fair few rivals need a personal best.

Captain’s Pick has solid recent form, winning two starts ago and running well since. Handles the trip and ground well, and benefits from the capable hands of jockey David Noonan. Represents trainer Christian Williams, who’s in good form. A fair each-way punt with strong potential for placing or winning.

The model I run suggests an upset from Sporty Jim. Sporty Jim lines up here with the joint highest RPR of this 11-horse race but also has the lowest official ranking. This means Sporty Jim carries the lowest amount of weight around this 2m 7f trip. The price here is high, offers plenty of value, and if you prefer each way betting, some value could be taken from 19s. The model has issued a very low stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Has some winning form back in 2022/23. Has been disappointing since, but now looks on a very nice handicap mark and has recently changed trainer.
Hurdles winner who is yet to win from 5 starts over fences but did finish 2nd at Uttoxeter last time. Every chance if building on that performance.
Perhaps we should all be scared of the Owen Switcher, but he hasn't had it long. This one looked stretched by 3m last time out, but I'm convinced he has a race in him.

The Luck is one that can act on any going. It has 5 wins on good and has won on soft and heavy. Drops in class after finding it tough at Warwick last time when the ground was almost firm. Gets this trip and Beau Morgan, who is 2/3 on him, gets back in the saddle.
Fairly disappointing in 5 starts over hurdles and finished 3rd of 5 on chasing debut last time. Should be better than previous races have shown, and any improvement would give an each-way chance.
Followed up third on debut with a fourth here in Worcester last month. Now makes the step up to hurdling, so interested to see if he can justify favouritism.

The model I run suggests an upset here by Spartan Times. This result has been driven by Spartan Times having the highest RPR in this 9-horse race. Spartan Times is the youngest horse here and looks the most progressive. Good 5th 32 days ago and would have come on well from that experience. William Shanahan on board relieves a further 5 lbs off the weight being carried, which takes the total down to the lowest of all runners here. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Up to a career-high mark today. But her overall form suggests she can cope with this type of mark.
She's run 2 solid races the last twice. On her penultimate run, she ran a nice enough race behind Verace Twentyone. Beaten 3L by the winner. She was giving 10lbs in weight to the winner.
She ran a cracker last time out. Beaten just 3L by the winner Super Sabre Sam, back in 2nd place. A rock-solid effort behind the well-handicapped winner.
She goes back against her own sex this time. She should appreciate the return to her own sex this time, having run so well against the lads last time out.
This is the trainer's sole runner at this meeting today. They usually do well with their runners at this track.
Won her last race with a positive ride. Should do the same this time. Distance is no problem. Jockey claiming five pounds should lead all the way. Great each way chance at 6/1.

Going to dutch in this race both selections will be each way but I can't do them like that on here so one will be win. Versace Twentyone is the first pick, last run can be forgiven before that she is a consistent mare. 14/1
Would have needed the run at Aintree last month following a lengthy absence of 250 days. Won over this trip at Uttoxeter 3 races ago off a mark of 110 and just a pound higher today.

Lovis De Sceaux shaped well last time out, finishing second, showing clear signs of progression. Lightly raced and improving with experience. Backed by an in-form jockey and trainer combination. Excellent value compared to the shorter-priced favourite. Ground and trip look ideal. A strong contender with win potential.
Stayed on well to win over this course and distance on debut in April. Likely to improve for having had that run and should be there or thereabouts.
Won last time out, so has to be considered. Although this is a huge step up in class and has a penalty, there's obvious potential here.
Well backed last time and ran as if he can win from this sort of mark. New headgear added in the hope to eke out that little bit of improvement.
Ran on well when third over a furlong further on the Wolverhampton tapeta under today's jockey last time out, will welcome the drop in trip and the forecast rain.

Sir Benedict has not won yet this year, but last month did manage to take a decent second in the last 100 yards. This makes me think he could improve now, stepping up to 6 furlongs while still on a mark of 46, with his last win being around this time last year off a 54.

Just one win from 26 runs and going through a barren run with 15 runs without a win, as the last win was last year. But did show encouraging signs LTO when finishing 4th of 10 at Bath and should be able to be competitive off the current mark.

Has to bounce back from a poor reappearance run last time, but his form from last year is very good. He is well thought of by connections and has plenty of stamina in his pedigree. Class horse of the race.

These three-year-old handicaps are very difficult to work out as the participants are maturing at different rates and often stepping up to trips that they are going to be best at. One trainer who has a very good record in this category of races is Andrew Balding, and he sends the progressive-looking Way Of Stars in search of his maiden victory. Both runs this season have shown plenty of promise, and the step up to a mile and three-quarters is almost certainly the biggest hint that a win is in the offing.
Has improved in each of 3 starts and was a winner at Haydock last time. Remains open to further improvement and likely to be there or thereabouts.

I’m not expecting the blinkers to aid Anniversary at all here given Sea The Moon’s poor 7% SR (A/E 0.44) with their use. Half-brother to the favourite, Way Of Stars, is another you can oppose due to A Balding’s 6% SR (A/E 0.41) with his progeny, meanwhile J Boyle is having a torrid season so far (5% SR, A/E 0.43) so I couldn’t have much faith in Many Men returning to winning ways. C Johnston does awful with handicap debutants (9% SR, A/E 0.6) so Pole Star shouldn’t be competitive, but PANTILE WARRIOR could improve to no end with the hood given how well the Gosden’s utilise the headgear (28% SR, A/E 1.31) and looks worth a chance at 15/2 (each way). The son of Frankel has been relatively disappointing so far with one win and three 2nds from seven starts but he’s no forlorn hope and the booking of B De La Sayette is a positive given his 20% SR (A/E 1.4) on pear-shaped courses.

Could go well at a price. Have to overlook his last effort, but the form of his 2nd at Sandown last September is right up there form-wise. Certainly, that performance was much better than his mark of 82, so he has an each-way chance.

This is a lightly-raced winner. With cheekpieces applied for the first-time, he achieved a commendable 5th place out of 7 in a handicap at Thirsk 3 weeks ago. He should not be ruled out as he increases his trip, particularly given the excellent form of both the trainer and jockey. Still, at enticing odds of 25/1, an each-way wager seems to be the wisest option.
Previous course and distance winner. Goes on all ground so is versatile. Only 1lb above last winning mark and should have a good chance here.
Billyjoh came into form last time at Leicester and hasn't won for a while so looks on a handy weight in this handicap with conditions to suit.
Won over this trip on the 21st of April and will welcome the drop in trip and ease in grade after 2 races over a mile in Class 2. This Class 3 should me more suitable.
Shark Two One went third final stride over 7 furlongs at Leicester 11 days ago and could go well dropping in trip.
Now 7lb below last winning mark. Drops another 2 for a 6th place finish last time out at Thirsk. Versatile on the ground should it turn to soft conditions. Solid each way.

Last Chance Saloon for this one, who drops down to his lowest ever mark. Needs everything to drop right as he seems to find trouble. His last 2 races running into trouble. 12s is a price worth taking a chance with.

Tailorman looks well placed in this Class 5 handicap, with strong staying form and an ideal draw. Jim Crowley takes the ride, signaling confidence. Ian Williams targets these races well, and the horse should be suited by pace and ground. A leading contender, capable of seeing this out strongly.
The only C&D winner in the field and now dropping to what looks like a very tempting mark. Ran okay on return at York over a shorter trip than this. Could prove hard to beat.

This won't take a lot of winning and Grand Voyage looks solid. He had been running well in better races than this before being stretched by 3m last time out. He drops in class and in trip, has run well at the track, and the likely soft ground suits.

The model I run suggests Ballydangan could win this one. Ballydangan lines up here with the highest RPR of the 12-runner field but has an official ranking leaving him right down the bottom in terms of weight being carried. This gap between running potential and weight being carried over the 2m 4f distance might be telling by the finish line. Peter Kavanagh on board relieves a further 3 lbs, which helps. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

His two runs this year have been poor but he finished in the top 3 in 5 of his 6 runs last year. It is concerning that his only Chase win came in January 2022 but he is 38lbs lower today and should run well.
Completed a hat trick of wins when winning at Kelso last month. 7 lb higher today, but that should be manageable and likely to be there or thereabouts.

The model I run suggests Powers Dilemma has a good chance of getting over the line first here. This result has been driven by Powers Dilemma having an RPR comparable to the rest of the field, but an official ranking much lower than the other 4 runners in this 5 horse race. This subsequently means Powers Dilemma carries significantly less weight around this 2m 7f trip. Good form coming into this, with a second place finish 18 days ago. Peter Kavanagh on board relieves a further 3 lbs and that might just be the difference at the end. There is a total weight gap of 2 stone to the current market favourite, and that kind of weight difference over ~3m is surely telling. The model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator, which translates to a 1pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Comes into this off the back of a solid run last time out. The first bit of form she's shown in a good while. She's left on the same mark this time, stepping up in distance.
She finished a solid 3rd at this track last time out, with the first-time blinkers on. She was only beaten just over 4 lengths by the winner, Miss Maverick. That form's been franked by the winner, who went up 5 lbs for that win and won again next time out, bolting up by 6 lengths.
This step up in trip is what she needs. Both career wins come over this distance. The forecast rain will only enhance her chances, in my opinion. The blinkers she ran a cracker in last time out are left on again. Hopefully, they can help her get her head back in front.

I don't think one should be the outsider in this field. Had 2 quick runs last month, so should be fit. Gets reunited with Jones, who rode him the last time he won. He also won't mind if the ground goes soft.

Surrey Belle had two wins over hurdles in February before flopping in her first handicap in March at Kelso. She has since run two close 2nd places on the flat and should be ready to show she is worthy of her handicap hurdle mark.

The model I run suggests Mack The Man can win this one. Mack The Man lines up with the highest RPR of the 10-runner field and has an official ranking leaving him in the middle of the pack. Carries less weight for that and is one of the few showing form coming into this one. Good 2nd place 23 days ago, looks to go one better here. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Although he has a better record over fences, this is his first run over hurdles since March 2023 and this is his lowest mark since August 2023 when he won at Cartmel. He won off a 1lb higher mark at Newcastle last November and could improve here.

The model I run suggests Wee Alki can win this one. This result has been driven by Wee Alki having the highest RPR of the 16-runner race and an official ranking, leaving her carrying a middle to high amount of weight. Comes here with good form figures and was unlucky not to come first in the last race. 243-22 and looking to add a 1 to those numbers, Rebekah Duffy picks up the reins and relieves a further 7 lbs. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

TINY ANGEL is one of two entries making the journey across from Ireland. This one could be the more likely apparently more forward and racing over a hurdles trip in handicap company which should suit she rates a decent value option.

Went second close to home over course and distance last time out. Remains on the same mark but Alice Stevens takes the ride today and her 5 pound allowance could prove valuable to help Community Rebel making a winning stable debut for Micky Hammond.
Sean Og did well when last here in October when running off a 100 in a C5. He won a C4 on the return in February off the same mark and is only 2 lbs higher today.

The model I run suggests Dr. Shirocco could win this one and cause an upset. Not too fancied by the early market, so 10s can offer some value. The result has been driven by Dr. Shirocco having the second highest RPR of the field, but carries over 2 stone (!) less than the top weight, and 1.5 stone difference to the current market favorite. If the horse runs to its potential, that should be far too much of a weight gap not to show by the end of this longer 3m distance. Add to that, Dr. Shirocco is a prior course and distance winner, ran a good 3rd 18 days ago, so comes here with some kind of form. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator for this, driven by a combination of the small gap back to second in the race simulation, but 10s offering good value for the win probability % predicted by the model. This translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Not really shown much in the last three races, although the latest was a bit better. Managed to complete. Looks to be on a good mark. If bouncing back to form, should make the frame.

This is a very light data race and so possibly a rogue output. The model has suggested Owt For Nowt at 51s to win. Have to take at face value given prior long shot winners in the past. The model result has been driven by Owt For Nowt carrying the lowest amount of weight around this 2m trip. There is a full stone in weight difference to the top of the market and only horse to have previously run, Mancero. 51s is a monster price and in a 5 horse race where 4 haven't run before, seems worth the risk. Very low stake indicator, as a result of the uncertainty. 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
First win in 2 years and has found his form dropped in grade. Comes here, down further in grade from just 3 lb higher, which is negated by his jockey's claim. Should follow up.

Probably a touch too high in the weights to win this but she loves this C&D, three wins and a couple of further places here. Four of her eight career wins have come under this jockey so his return after nine runs without him could help her find enough to at least hit the frame.
Was a winner at Newcastle on final start for previous yard in October. Disappointed on first start for this yard but has ability and holds an each-way chance.
Has won over this course and distance. Disappointing last time out, but seems to love this course, so could well produce a nice run.
Good win at Wolverhampton last time out and in with a decent chance returning to handicaps off what looks like an acceptable mark.

LHEBAYEB looks to have a solid chance returning to the turf here. She returns here from a lower grade and weight than she was at last season so could pinch this. Had some handy looking runs this year and is forgiven for the last time out showing as it was a touch up in class.

John O'Shea LTO Winners at Chepstow - 33.3% SR, 1.51 A/E, +£28.85 LSP to £1 Stake. Yard can be backed blind at Chepstow in last 12 months, 17.29%, +£13 LSP to £1 Stake. 5-time Course Winner. Up 2 lbs for recent win when overcoming a slow start and mid-race switch. Best Run-Out Speed in the field at 35.54 mph. Gina Mangan 22.9% SR in Chepstow Sprints, 1.68 A/E, +10.96 LSP to £1 Stake.
Lost second towards the finish when 3rd of 9, beaten half a length over 6 furlongs here last time out. Should appreciate the drop in trip.
A case can be made for Level Up to go close, who has always run well during the summer months and is very well treated on winning sprint form over this minimum trip.

Unlucky not to finish closer last time when meeting trouble in running. Won in a slightly higher grade off the same mark a year ago and won from 2lb higher on AW in November. Looks a solid each-way bet.

Her recent performances include a 4th-place finish at York on May 31 over 7f, where she was beaten by just 2 lengths . Prior to that, she finished 6th at Haydock on May 22 over 6f 212y, only 2.5 lengths behind the winner. Earlier in May, she placed 8th at Kempton over 6f, showing consistency in competitive fields. 
Miss Collada's pedigree (Mehmas ?- Kocollada) suggests aptitude for sprint distances, and her previous victories at Salisbury and Wolverhampton over 5f indicate she possesses the speed to be competitive . With the step up to 7f and the return to turf, she presents as a solid each-way proposition at likely generous odds.

A beaten favourite when second in a Class 5 under an 8 pound claimer over course and distance last time out. Eased in grade to Class 6 and could go one better in this company in the more experienced hands of Jack Doughty.

Despite being on the cold list, this trainer's runners are going much better recently and only just missing out. This horse will be fitter after a spin on the AW last time out, and she can go close here with the forecast rain improving her chances no end. She won on soft last year and is only 2 lb higher now. Her other run on soft saw her beaten less than 2 lengths too, so the conditions are likely to play to her strengths here.

My vote to take this class 6 handicap will be going to Adrian who was last seen at Wolverhampton 19 days ago where finishing a respectable 7th/12 that was his seasonal reappearance run after a 221 day break having also exchanged ownership in the process of that break and is most certainly entitled to strip fitter with that run under his belt drops in trip racing at 1 mile 4 furlong trip here that being of no concern and this drop in trip is likely to suit well having found a race that should also suit his nature of going perfectly well given the horses enrolled to run here currently operating on a mark of 51 B J Llewellyn's inmate looks poised to strike here and ticks all boxes to do so jockey Aidan Keeley takes the ride and can give Adrian a promising ride here at Chepstow
Should strip fitter for 2 runs in the last 6 weeks following a 4 month break. The drop in trip and class should suit having raced over 7 furlongs in a Class 5 here last time out.
Has scored 2 wins over C&D, but she is currently out of form. At least her last win was off a higher mark, so a return to this course and a drop down in class gives her strong claims for an upset.
Has a sixth and seventh to their name so far, so needs some improvement. The recent rain could help make some progress.
All previous 9 runs have been on the all-weather, with the only win coming in February. Form has dipped since then but drops in trip for turf debut and holds an each-way chance.

Divot is a real interest and his large E/W odds at the time of writing was last seen at Newbury 22 days ago where finishing 11th/14 however that was just his second outing after a 196 day break and he looked in need of both the outing and the experience and he certainly gained both fitness and experience from that run at the very least currently operating on a mark of 62 this gelded son of Footstepsinthesand & Western Pearl ( Dam's sire High Chaparral ) is likely to capable of much better in very good time and he can begin to trouble the judge so is not one to underestimate trainer William Knight has a healthy £10.69 profit to a 1 level stake when having just the one runner at a flat meeting and Divot is capable of enhancing that statistic further jockey Neil Callan takes the ride and can ensure Divot gets the best possible outcome here must enter calculations and shouldn't be by any means underestimated . Respected .
Has finished 2nd twice and 3rd once from last 3 starts. Step up in trip should suit and likely to be there or thereabouts.
Improved on a solid debut performance to finish 3rd at Wolverhampton. Further improvement is likely on turf debut and holds an each-way chance.

Salamanca City is taken to follow up a nice win at Haydock over ten furlongs recently with a win in this same grade (Class 4) contest closer to home at Lingfield. James Fanshawe (SR 22%) stable in form. Rain would help. Kaiya Fraser (SR 24%)'s 3lbs claim will help. She's a nicely bred filly by Phoenix Of Spain out of a Dubawi mare and can continue to progress.
Party Island last won in July off a 67 in a C5. Last month he was fourth here, just over a length away from the winner, and goes again off the same mark of 68 but with a 7 lbs claimer on top.
Has shown some improved form for this yard and was a winner for the first time at Brighton last time. Up 5lb, but that is likely to be manageable and holds every chance of following up.

Trained by Patrick Owens, this three-year-old filly has shown consistent form, finishing third in her last two starts at Doncaster over similar distances and ground conditions .
Her recent performances suggest she's on the cusp of a breakthrough, and the return to turf could play to her strengths. The booking of Jack callan using his claim adds further confidence for this selection.
Dianarina finished last in its last race. However, it's now tried in a combination of first-time blinkers and a hood, which could have an effect at a very large price. So, worth the risk.

Havanita, a 3-year-old filly by Havana Gold, is entered in the 7f Restricted Maiden Stakes at Lingfield and will be ridden by George Bass, a notable booking for the day . Trained by Patrick Chamings and owned by Mrs R. Lyon & Chamings, she steps back onto turf following a 9th-place finish in a 7f novice event at Kempton on May 21 .
That Kempton run??'just 17 days ago??'offered little in the way of promise, but this return to turf could unlock latent potential. Her breeding (Havana Gold ?- Buttercross) suggests mile aptitude, and this drop into a restricted race may bring her into play. George Bass’s ride adds confidence; his familiar partnership with Chamings may provide the tactical edge.
Lingfield’s good to firm going should suit her, and with only 10 in this field, she has a chance to be prominent throughout. While not a standout on paper, the booking of Bass and the switch from AW to turf give her each-way appeal at likely attractive odds.

Blue Collar Lad is a bit tricky but has won on the turf here and will have no problem with the softening ground. The interesting angle with him is first-time blinkers. He won when wearing cheekpieces for the first time. The cheekpieces were removed for 4 starts, and then he won again when they were reapplied. He also ran well in Jersey, finishing half a length second in a first-time visor. First-time blinkers could be the time to catch him, and he's very well handicapped.
Promising start to its career without winning, but today it's dropped in trip, which should suit. From top stable with good jockey up.
Showed plenty of promise on debut at Naas last month when finishing 2nd. Likely to improve on that performance and could go 1 better.

Stock Market is a 2yo colt trained by A P O'Brien. He is sired by No Nay Never (USA), who went unbeaten as a 2yo winning three times including a group 1, he is out of a dam trained by Roger Varian, who also won on debut. He is a full brother to Rizg, also trained by Roger Varian, who also won on 2yo debut, and a half-brother to the 117-rated Hotazhell, a four-time winner as a 2yo, winning three group races and finishing third in this year's Irish 2000 Guineas. So, Stock Market comes from a very precocious pedigree line and should go close on debut under Ronan Whelan.

The model I run suggests this is Joueur Masque to win. This result has been driven by Joueur Masque having the second highest RPR of the runners here, where the majority of horses carry the same initial amount of weight. Gavin Brouder on board relieves 3 lbs, and that could be helpful. The biggest risk here is Joueur Masque has not run in 183 days, and race fitness may be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Made his racecourse debut at odds of 125/1 in a 17f novice at Down Royal. Wasn’t beaten far in 4th and looked set to step up on that performance when coming to grief at Fairyhouse last time. Starts out for a new yard here, back down in trip, and is worth a second look.

Arch Empire has been in good form of late with a win and a runner-up finish inside the last 3 outings. Sandwiched in between them was another outing where it was a faller when within touching distance 2 from home as well.

Receiving all the allowances from the boys here, I reckon Belle The Tigress has some ability and could make a mockery of some of these (hopefully all of them). The penny looks to have finally dropped for her, and hopefully, she can confirm my hopes today. I'll be on weather watch as good ground looks to be important for her.
Timeless Treaty has only had one run but won that, with the second that day going on to win since. So I would expect more today, now second up, with the same 7 lbs claiming rider.
In best form of his life and the 8 lbs increase for his latest win might not be enough to stop him achieving the hat-trick here.

The model I run suggests Meehall can win this one. Meehall lines up here with the second highest RPR of this large 19-runner race, but carries a relatively lower amount of weight on this longer 3m stamina test. Comes here in decent form, 131P-3 figures, and if anywhere near the best, can come first again here. G Noonan on board relieves a further 5 lbs, which helps. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which is driven by the small gap to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Western Model was beaten six and a half lengths by Riggs in his latest race over a similar distance but now has a fifteen pound pull in the weights and could turn the tables with seven pound claimer Peter Smithers taking the ride.

I genuinely feel there could be a race to be won with Paddy Kelly’s 9-year-old gelding FRIENDS N COMMERCE. I know it’s a bold statement, given this son of SHOLOKHOV is still a maiden after 23 runs - but if he is to break that duck, it won’t be on good ground. With rain forecast, conditions could finally fall in his favour.
He’s placed twice at Punchestown from four runs and was only a length off the winner over this trip on yielding ground - off a hurdle mark of 109. He runs today over fences off 104, so he’s 5lbs better in. That could be significant.
The booking of UK-based jockey Aaron Anderson is intriguing. He’s over for just two rides??'both for this yard - and claims a useful 5lbs. He’s hit the frame with 28.57% of his rides in the past fortnight. The trainer has a solid 33.33% place strike rate here over the past five years.
If more rain arrives, it’ll only help. At a current price of 20/1, I’m happy to have some skin in the game. It could go wrong, sure - but there’s just enough in the profile to justify a small, hopeful punt.

QUEEN OF THUNDER in addition holds a Group 1 entry and brings the confidence oif a seasonal reappearance maiden win. She was seventh in last year's 1,000 Guineas at Newmarket and clearly aiming high as a four year old she merits respect.
The market leader looks too short here and so for some better value I am going to go with Barnavara who placed last time out, has won over this trip and could easily place again today.

Spicy Margarita is a 3-year-old filly trained by Adrian Murray. She has a bit to find on ratings but has a lovely pedigree, being related to six individual winners, two of which posted career-high RPR of 109-112. She is out of a dam called Nahoodh, trained by Mark Johnston, who won the Group 1 Falmouth Stakes and was rated 115. If reproducing the fast-finishing fourth in the 1m Group 3 Park Express Stakes over a mile at the Curragh in April, when beaten just 2.25 lengths, she could outrun current odds today under J M Sheridan.

Davy Crockett, a son of Annie Power and Camelot, makes his long-awaited debut at Punchestown today for JP McManus and Willie Mullins. There are very strong rumors the horse is ready to win first time out. What more can I say! Annie Power was a terrific mare in her racing days, and it will be fabulous to see her son take this race on the way to better things.

The model I run suggests Our Sonny should win this. It has the highest RPR and lines up with the same initial amount of weight as most of the other runners. Mr. Ryan on board relieves a further 7 lbs, which brings the weight total down to the bottom of the runners. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Muted Melody is a bit of a punt as I like having Jody Townend in the saddle. But she does have Faugheen in her relations and could go well first up EW.

MASKARVEL comes from a yard who know what it takes to land a Bumper winner sometimes with some bets also. This newcomer cost enough to think he could be up to the task first-up and the market can often be the best guide to the most likely outcome in races of this nature.
Not seen since November but placed in all of the last 3 outings. Holds every chance if returning in the same form.

A chance is taken with Sturlasson, a 4yo gelding trained by Kieran P Cotter, who is a CD winner on today's good ground, posting a RPR of 92. Then finished 2/19 on next start at Epsom, posting a career-high RPR of 94. Runs today off a mark of 79, so clearly well handicapped under Chris Hayes and the return Navan could revive. Kieran P Cotter also does well in 5f handicap sprints at Navan, winning with 8 of his last 29 runners. Interesting!

Irish Rumour is a 5-year-old mare trained by Miss Jennifer Anne Lynch, a trainer amongst the winners of late, winning with Arctic Steps at 66-1. Her other runners have been found well. Irish Rumour is a CD winner on today's good ground and is 5lb higher on 67 but has posted a career-high RPR of 78, so the mark is workable. Backed off the boards last time out when finishing 2/20 at Naas under Colin Keane (riding in the Derby), beaten a head behind today's favourite but is 2lb better off today. A big run was clearly expected last time out, and Irish Rumour can make amends today.

Former course and distance winner Bobbing About in the market. Handicap mark in fast freefall descent from 67 in April to a mark of 55 three races later. Now ten pounds below course and distance winning mark from September. Rather intriguing at a nice price.

Nouvel Espoir has been a bit down the pack of late but did win last August off today's mark. He has had a run on the return last week, which was again to midfield, but will be all the better for it. I would expect more now, second up with a 10 lbs claimer in the saddle. EW 4P.

The model I run suggests Sysko can win this race. Sysko lines up here with the second highest RPR of this very large 21-horse race but isn't penalized for it in the weights. Practically all horses carry the same initial weight. The big thing to flag here is Sysko has not run in 313 days, so will need to go well fresh here to have the chance. Sean Cleary-Farrell on board relieves 7 lbs, which can help on the 2m 3f trip. The model issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Has shown winning form in the past and has been there or thereabouts in recent runs, so hoping for a step up here today.

Treasure Rose should build on an encouraging debut when slowly away at Gowran Park. Murtagh has a good record when it comes to races like this between 8f and 12f. Market confidence would underline this one but I am going to trust it.
Was third on debut in similar going, and that was in a non-handicap too. The poor performance last time out was attributed to being lame, so could improve again here.

Seemed to better market expectations on her debut at Navan when 5th of 20 over 10f. Was doing her best work at the finish and ran to a similar level at Gowran last time despite appearing to be unsuited by the drop in trip. Back up in distance can see her reward each way support before going down the handicap route.

Still a maiden after 7 chase runs, but this P2P winner has done enough to suggest this type of mark should be within range. He comes into this with a bit to prove at present, having struggled in much better races than this the last twice. The most recent being at this track, he pulled up 2 from home in the latter race having never got involved. His best chase run to date came at Leopardstown. He finished an eye-catching 3rd in a pretty strong race, beaten just 7L by the winner Jeannot Lapin. He had lots of subsequent winners beaten off in behind him despite never being put into the race. He ran a solid race over CD in a listed novice hurdle race behind Tullyhill, beaten 9L by the winner albeit. To be fair, that rates decent form given the winner is a Grade 1 placed horse. The jockey takes off 7lbs here. This drop back in trip should suit him.
Solitary Man brings stronger 2 mile credentials. He has the better tactical speed, and is well handicapped on peak novice form.

Gaelic Arc has been running in some decent races and has been dropping in the handicap. Two miles is more his distance than the staying chase he ran in last time and he has a good chance of at least a place.

The model I run suggests Kalnoo can win this one. Kalnoo lines up here with the joint second highest RPR of this large 20-horse race and has an official ranking, leaving it very well treated in the weights. Steps out with the second lowest amount of weight to carry and has shown some reasonable form coming into this. Figures of 3335-4 and comes here after last running 16 days ago, so race fitness should not be a concern.
