Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, and this translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Was a winner at Fairyhouse on penultimate start in October. Ran with credit last time and holds an each-way chance if returning in the same form.

FORTUNE THE BRAVE is interesting on his handicap debut taking in this more extreme distance. Connections will have learned something from his recent latest qualifying effort over a similar trip and this opening mark would appear on the lenient side.

Pretty open handicap hurdle race over three miles. Butchers Bill has put in fair efforts the last twice off quite a high handicap mark. Finn Brickley's 7 lbs claim is going to help. Gordon Elliott (SR 21%) amongst the winners, as is the jockey. Kayf Tara 5yo will want a staying trip and probably would be better for rain. Saw market support prior to being pulled from a race recently. Interesting.

Impressive 2nd out of 6 in a novice hurdle at Wexford a mere 10 days ago. This experienced 7 year old, under the guidance of the in-form Conor O'Dwyer, is expected to deliver a strong performance, and the 5lb claim from the jockey will be beneficial. With enticing odds of 28/1, this could yield a substantial each-way return.
This is trainers only entry he's got out today as they are stepping it back up in trip with an interesting 3lbs claiming jockey booking / change, a good value ew bet for the 5 places available.

ASHLIA DANCER is an out-of-season racer at least in good form. A nine year old mare who has presumably had her issues through her career and with just seven races under rules she could be the right yype to have on side in this staying handicap hurdle.

I’ve bored anyone who’ll listen with my ramblings about how hard it is to pick a winner - never mind trying to preempt the weather, or more precisely, how much rain actually seeps into the ground. That said, the forecast says it’s raining overnight and for a good chunk of tomorrow in County Kildare, which could turn this good/yielding ground soft. And if that happens, I’d give a tentative shout to Denise Foster’s 10-year-old gelding, RIDEAU CANAL.
This lad has shown only snippets of form - three places from 15 starts - but all have come on soft ground. He kept on well for third at both Fairyhouse (20f) and Sligo (21f), the latter off a mark of 88. He lines up here today 11lbs lower. That Sligo run came last August, and hasn’t had preferred conditions since.
Foster has a 25% place strike rate here the past five years. Jockey Kevin Sexton mirrors that strike rate, and you’d be in profit if you’d backed all his rides here blindly over the same period.
If it rains and turns soft - maybe, we’ve got a squeak. If it doesn’t? Run away. Don’t back him, not even with stolen money.

Highly rated Gerard Keane (SR 20%) stable had a recent winner over a staying trip. Ragmans Corner ran a solid third, beaten less than a length, on recent return to action and first Flat handicap start. Has had success over hurdles, running out a 12 length winner at Punchestown in January. This 6yo is unexposed on the Flat and could easily come on for recent outing. Jack Kearney claims a 3lbs allowance.
Not seen since September but has won 3 of the last 4 races. Has at least an each-way chance if returning in the same form.

Lightly raced for his age and has finished placed in both of his handicaps so far on the flat. Last time out was over this trip at Gowran, shaping as if the stiffer track at the trip on similar ground and off the same mark will be a help.

BURREN SONG is three times a turf winner and is feasibly treated with an upwardly-mobile 7lb claiming apprentice aboard. That reads well for this seven year old mature multi-purpose racer's chance and in a competitive middle-distance Saturday handicap he rates the value play.

APOLOGISE is another multi-purpose operator who is not fully exposed as a flat racer and he could prove a very well treated runner in this sphere. He aslo has the distinct advantage of Sam Coen's 7lb claim who seems to be used more sparingly to preserve the claim he still holds and he could surprise.
Was a winner for the first time at Down Royal in June last year but failed to build on that when last seen in July. Holds an each-way chance if rediscovering that form on return.
